thread:
Alex: heads-up — us-south1 GPU attach queue is backed up, lots of attach-waits. I see sustained write-tail spikes on local disks of mixed-node class (older and newer NVMe together). Nodes showing high iowait and long kv-cache evictions.
Maya: on it. which hosts and any quick logs?
Alex: hosts: gnode-us-south1-{12..19}. dmesg shows write timeout chatter. quick iostat snapshot: 
```
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00  25.00  12.4  540.0  98.0  27680   100.0    10.2   148.3   8.6  160.1  1.85  99.7
```
Also saw overlayfs snapshots getting churned by background cleanup jobs.
Sam: those numbers smell like tinywrite-heavy work (4k write burst) + background janitor compaction. mixed firmware on same rack amplifies tail cats.
Ops-Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3141 - "storage write-tail causing GPU attach holds (us-south1)". Pager: eng-oncall.
Teja: temporary mitigation idea: throttle janitor and snapshot frequency on the affected nodes, or migrate batch jobs off the mixed nodes. Can we set janitor.rate=0.5 and reduce snapshot cadence to 10m?
Dmitri: prefer throttling over stop. stopping janitor risks accumulation of small files. Use `systemctl set-property janitor.service CPUQuota=50%` + `janitor.rate=0.5` for a few hours.
Maya: I pushed a quick change: reduced snapshot cadence and applied janitor rate to 0.4 on 8 hosts. Observed attach success rate jump 40% -> 92% within 5min.
Alex: also disabled overlayfs per-node snapshotting on two worst hosts, remounted writable. attach latency dropped sharply.
Sam: post-mortem action: need a perf test that reproduces 4k random write + overlayfs snapshot + janitor compaction on mixed-firmware NVMe. Capture fio traces and blktrace to isolate whether firmware GC or host GC is dominant.
Maya: added remediation checklist to INC-2026-3141: cordon mixed nodes for large batch, schedule firmware parity for those racks, create SLO alert for local device avgqu-sz > 5 for >2m.
Alex: thanks all — will keep an eye, rolling migration now. Will follow up with runbook updates. :thumbsup:
